name: adverbs
title: Spanish Adverbs Practice: -mente, Frequency and Place Quiz
description: Practice Spanish adverbs: -mente adverbs, frequency (siempre, nunca), place, time and bien vs bueno, with a rule table and 10 checked sentences.
answer: Many Spanish adverbs add -mente to the feminine form of the adjective: lento → lentamente, rápido → rápidamente, fácil → fácilmente. Common adverbs have their own form: bien, mal, siempre, nunca, aquí, allí, ya, todavía. Adverbs of frequency usually go before or right after the verb, and nunca before the verb needs no extra no.

demand.source: Google autocomplete for US searchers (hl=en, gl=us), docs/seo-plan/us1000/suggest-us-20261127b.csv

rules.use: Two in a row: -mente only on the last

rules.example: siempre, a menudo, a veces, casi nunca, nunca
aquí, allí, cerca, lejos; ya, todavía, pronto, tarde

quiz.why: -mente goes on the feminine form: lenta → lentamente.
To modify a verb, use the adverb bien, not the adjective bueno.
The adjective fácil keeps its accent: fácilmente.
Nunca before the verb works alone.
After no + verb, Spanish uses nada, not algo: no me gusta nada.

quiz.before: El profesor explicó la lección clara y
quiz.why: With two adverbs, only the last takes -mente.
Place adverbs like cerca have no -mente.

quiz.after: va al gimnasio: dos o tres veces por semana.
quiz.why: Two or three times a week is often: a menudo.

quiz.after: come verduras; solo le gusta la pizza.
quiz.why: Only liking pizza means almost never: casi nunca.

mistakes: Adding -mente to the masculine form: «rápidomente» should be «rápidamente».
Using bueno instead of bien: «cantas bueno» should be «cantas bien».
Adding no before nunca at the start: «no nunca como carne» should be «nunca como carne» or «no como carne nunca».
Putting -mente on both adverbs: «clara y lentamente» is the natural form, not «claramente y lentamente».
Dropping the accent: fácilmente, rápidamente and últimamente keep the accent of the adjective.

heritage: Heritage speakers often use short adverbs like rápido and fuerte without -mente (habla rápido), which is normal Spanish. In writing, check the accent on -mente adverbs that come from accented adjectives (fácilmente) and avoid the English «más mejor»: mejor already means better.
teacher: Students write their weekly routine with one frequency adverb per line (siempre, a menudo, a veces, nunca) and then find a classmate who matches three of their lines.

faq.question: How do you form adverbs with -mente?
faq.answer: Take the feminine singular of the adjective and add -mente: lenta → lentamente, feliz → felizmente. Adjectives that do not change for gender just add it: fácil → fácilmente, triste → tristemente.

faq.question: Where do adverbs of frequency go?
faq.answer: Usually before the verb (siempre llego temprano) or at the end of the sentence (llego temprano siempre). Nunca and casi nunca before the verb need no extra no.

faq.question: Is it bien or bueno?
faq.answer: Bien is an adverb and describes how something is done (cocinas bien). Bueno is an adjective and describes a noun (una comida buena). With estar, bien describes how someone is: estoy bien.
